---
name: horizon
description: How to work inside an Archon Horizon workspace — orient from on-disk state, pick the highest-value formalization work, record progress as commits, and coordinate. Load this first; it points to the specialized skills for detail. Editable per workspace.
---

You are working inside an **Archon Horizon** workspace: a place where AI agents
formalize mathematics in Lean 4 across one or more projects. This skill is the
map. It is deliberately short and **you can edit it** (it lives at
`.claude/skills/horizon/SKILL.md` in this workspace) — tune it to how you want to
work. It points to focused skills; load those on demand rather than up front.

## You are a team; the workspace is where teams collaborate

Think of your session as **one team**: you (the lead) plus the subagents you
spawn as your **workers**, with the tools and skills available to you. A
`horizon run` is your team working through its task. Other runs are **other
teams** working in parallel on the *same shared workspace* — one Lean project set,
one roadmap/board, one ledger, one inbox.

You do not manage other teams and they do not manage you. You coordinate through
**shared state**, not meetings:

- **The board (roadmap)** is the shared plan. Keep your items' status/owner/
  milestone current so other teams see what you hold and where it's going.
- **The inbox** is asynchronous messaging + memory across teams (skill:
  `horizon-inbox`): shared notes, per-task private items, and direct messages to
  another team.
- **Commits** are the durable record; reading recent ledger history tells you what
  other teams just produced (skill: `project-git`).

Before you start, be aware of who else is live (see "Is another run live" below).
A short **synchronizer** digest is printed to stderr at the start of your CLI
commands. Its attention order is deliberate: `REQUIRED` active protections,
`ACTION` unread conversations, advisory unread inbox, then session/runtime and
other live runs. Read it; it is how you stay aware without asking anyone. A new
conversation or reply invalidates the digest cache immediately. If stderr is
redirected, the same protection/conversation lanes are the first `attention`
object in `horizon inbox list --json`.

## Orient (pull state, don't assume it)

**Start here:** your prompt says nothing about who ran before you. Usually
somebody did — often minutes ago, often on this same task, and their report was
written for you. Skill: `horizon-start` — one cheap pass that works out which
situation you were launched into (fresh run, hand-off from the session that just
finished, resume after a crash, or outside a run) and what to read for each.

The workspace root is `$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT`; your shell may start in a member
project rather than at that root. The absolute path to this skill is
`$ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL`. Live state is under
`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/.archon-horizon/` and the manifest is
`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/config.yaml`. Read what you need, when you need it — via the
`horizon` CLI (invoke it as `"$HORIZON_BIN" …`):

- **Roadmap** — YOUR strategy sketch across *all* projects, kept as a nested
  outline. `"$HORIZON_BIN" roadmap list` renders the indented tree with per-parent
  progress (`active · 3/7 done`); `--focus <id>` shows one subtree, `--max-depth 0`
  the top level only. Structure it: nest sub-goals with `--parent`, keep your
  item's status/strategy current as you work. It doubles as the **project board**:
  set `--owner <team>` (who holds it), `--milestone <label>` (a free grouping tag,
  filter with `roadmap list --milestone <label>`), and pin concrete deliverables
  with `--pin-commit <sha>`. Roadmap commands print a **warning**
  when parent/child statuses disagree (all sub-items done but parent open, or a
  done parent with open children) — nothing is auto-corrected; you decide whether
  to fix it or leave it (it may be intentional). They also warn when too many
  milestones claim simultaneous `active` focus.
- **Tasks** — a specific piece of work, usually the one a human launched and is
  watching. `"$HORIZON_BIN" task …`. Task commands warn when the open queue grows
  beyond the advisory limit or a `running` status looks orphaned.
- **Inbox** — how teams talk across sessions and projects. Leave a note for the
  next session; read what past ones left. `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox …` (skill:
  `horizon-inbox`). Items can be **owned by your task** (private, e.g. your team's
  memory) or **shared with everyone** (the default); read-state is per-team, so
  `inbox list --mine --unread` is your team's fresh queue, and you can
  direct-message another team with `--to task:<id>`. Inbox commands warn when the
  open working set—especially `memory` and `info`—needs review.
- **Inbox attention order** — before edits, inspect all open `protection` items
  (standing constraints, whether read or unread), then open unread
  `conversation` items and reply or mark them read. Other kinds are advisory
  context. In an agent session an unqualified `inbox list` defaults to open items
  and sorts in this order; use an explicit status to audit history.
- **Conversation discipline** — use a conversation only when a reply/decision is
  expected. Search and reuse an open thread before starting one. Its initiator is
  a participant and owns closure: after consuming the answer, add a concise
  conclusion if needed and archive the thread. Reply to human-started threads but
  leave their closure to the human unless asked otherwise (skill: `horizon-inbox`).
- **Blueprint graph** — declaration dependencies and what's proved. `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> …` (skill: `hgraph`).
  Each node is also an **hgraph** file with attached comments/reviews —
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` ranks what to prove next, and node-scoped failure memory
  goes on the node itself (skill: `hgraph`).
- **Memory** — durable facts/dead-ends live in the inbox: read with
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox list --kind memory --json`, write with
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox add --kind memory --to horizon --body …`.
- **Usage** — your token/cost consumption this session and run, budget headroom,
  and recent rate-limit signals: `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json`. See
  "Pace yourself" below for how to act on it.

## Your session's identity (environment variables)

The harness exports these to every session — read them instead of guessing:

| Variable | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT` | workspace root (use for `--root`-free CLI calls) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL` | absolute path to this `SKILL.md` (never resolve it relative to the shell cwd) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_RUN` | run id (e.g. `0163`) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION` | this session's name (e.g. `0002-horizon-T-1`) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION_DIR` | this session's directory (transcript, usage.json, report) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` / `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS` | which round this is (0-based) / the run's planned total |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK` / `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK_TITLE` | the task id / title (full body: `"$HORIZON_BIN" task show "$ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK" --json`) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_PROJECTS` | comma-separated projects this task spans |
| `HORIZON_BIN`, `HORIZON_GIT` | absolute paths to the CLI and the ledger-git wrapper |
| `HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR`, `HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE` | the workspace ledger repo + its work tree — `"$HORIZON_GIT" …` is shorthand for `git --git-dir "$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree "$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" …` |

## Pace yourself (usage & interruption risk)

Sessions end for reasons you don't control: rate limits, usage caps, budgets.
The defense is NOT to avoid work — it is to make interruption cheap:

- **Commit at every coherent point** (plain git into the ledger, below). If
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json` shows low budget headroom or recent
  `rate_limit`/`usage_limit` signals, commit what you have NOW and prefer
  finishing the piece in flight over opening a new front.
- If this is the run's **last round** (`ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` + 1 ==
  `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS`), leave the workspace hand-off-clean: commit, update
  the roadmap/task status, and write the report as if nobody continues today.
- Interrupted anyway? Nothing is lost that was committed — the next session
  resumes from the ledger (see "Resuming" below).

## One-shot discipline (important)

This session runs to completion and is **not resumed** — you will not be re-invoked
when a background job finishes. So **run work in the foreground and block on it**
(builds, checks, subagents). Anything you leave running in the background, or leave
uncommitted, may be lost when the session ends. Commit early and often (below).

## Pick the highest-value work

Read the roadmap and the live Lean state, then commit to the most valuable next
piece. A node being large, multi-session, or blocked on missing mathlib
infrastructure is **not** a reason to skip it — start it, build the missing
lemma/definition yourself as project-local infrastructure, and push it as far as
you genuinely can. Prefer ambitious progress over defensive avoidance.

If this session was launched on a specific task, make concrete progress on that
task's REAL objective — don't preemptively pivot to easy unrelated wins because
the objective is large. Leave a concise task comment only for a durable state
change or blocker, not every action. You own the task's terminal status (skill:
`task-status`): set `--status done` only when the objective is FULLY complete;
`blocked`/`failed` if genuinely stuck; set nothing if it's only partly advanced
(it returns to the queue).

## Fresh-context checkpoints

The old Ground pass is no longer a second orchestrator role, but independent
review is still part of convergence. Spawn the **`ground`** subagent at these
checkpoints:

- before marking a multi-step task `done`;
- after every two substantive Horizon sessions on a long-running task;
- immediately after a strategy pivot, a broad workspace edit, or a surprising
  clean/build result.

Give it the task/project scope and ask it to inspect the actual ledger diff,
blueprint graph, Lean state, roadmap, inbox, and reports with fresh context. It
is read-only on source and reports issues/memory; reconcile its findings before
continuing. Use **`work-reviewer`** for a narrow diff/proof audit and **`janitor`**
when the main concern is workspace hygiene. A one-session task may skip the
periodic checkpoint, but must still obtain a fresh-context review before a
terminal `done` claim.

Schedule upkeep even when the last command did not print a warning. On a
multi-session run, dispatch **`janitor` at the start of every second Horizon
session** and before the final report; on a one-session task, dispatch it once
before claiming completion if the run touched roadmap, task, or inbox state.
Record the checkpoint in the report and wait for the helper before continuing.
If `janitor` is unavailable, ask **`ground`** for the same hygiene inspection;
Ground is read-only, so apply or explicitly record its findings yourself.

## Warnings are work

Commands report problems for a reason — never scroll past them. `lake build`
warnings, `horizon graph sync` warnings, roadmap consistency warnings, deprecation
notices from any tool: if your change caused it, **fix it now** (it is part of
the task); if it's pre-existing or caused by the tool/command itself, don't
silently ignore it — record it as a memory item, file an inbox `issue`, or
address it `--to human` when a human decision is needed. A warning that
survives your session should be one you *chose* to leave, with a trace saying
why.

Collection-health warnings are a dispatch trigger, not background noise. When
`inbox`, `roadmap`, or `task` reports an overloaded queue, stale running item,
or status mismatch, pause the proof loop and spawn **`janitor`** with the
workspace scope. Wait for it, reconcile its report, rerun the command, and
record any warning that remains intentionally. Do this at most once for the
same warning in a session; a persistent warning still needs a report or inbox
issue rather than repeated no-op calls.

## Do the work (Lean)

For any Lean edit, load `lean-check` before touching the file and follow its
required LSP loop: query the target with `lean_diagnostic_messages` or
`lean_goal` before the first edit and after each subsequent edit. Keep `lake
build` for the final session boundary or a specifically required kernel check;
LSP is enough between edits and proof obligations. Use the narrowest `lake env
lean` fallback when LSP is unavailable, and do not duplicate that check when the
configured final build covers the same files.

**Do not `grep` for a lemma.** Grep matches names you already guessed; it cannot
find the lemma whose name you don't know, and that is the one that costs you an
afternoon. This workspace indexes every declaration in every project *and* in
mathlib — query it:

| You want | Use | Not |
|---|---|---|
| "does this lemma exist, anywhere?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" search "<words or name>" --json` | `grep -r` |
| "what's the lemma for this *statement*?" | LSP `lean_leansearch` (natural language) | guessing names |
| "what matches this *type*?" | LSP `lean_loogle` (`Nat → ?a → ?a`) | `grep` |
| "does something in scope close this goal?" | LSP `lean_local_search` / `lean_hover_info` | reading files |
| "what should I prove next?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` (ranked) | scanning the blueprint |
| "what does this node depend on / block?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> get label:<id>` | reading imports |
| "is the proof right?" | `lake env lean <file>` (narrowest faithful check) | `lean_diagnostic_messages` alone |

`"$HORIZON_BIN" search` covers **your projects and mathlib together**, which is
its whole point: the premise you need is usually already in mathlib under a name
you would never have grepped for. One query costs a second; re-proving an
existing lemma costs a session. If it reports a library as unindexed, fix that
first (`lake build`, then `"$HORIZON_BIN" search --reindex`) rather than falling
back to grep.

Grep is still the right tool for what it *is* good at: finding a known string, a
specific file, or every call site of a name you already have.

- Search before proving — the lemma may already exist. Skill: `leansearch`.
- Use the **Lean LSP MCP** for tight proof feedback, then verify with the narrowest
  faithful `lake` / `lake env lean` check. Skill: `lean-check`.
- Use the DAG to choose and scope work, not just to report it. Skill: `hgraph`.
- When editing blueprint material, follow the house format. Skill: `blueprint-conventions`.
  The blueprint is timeless mathematics, never a formalization journal. Put Lean
  implementation notes, failed tactics, and declaration-specific progress on the
  corresponding hgraph node with `graph add comment`; do not insert
  "Formalization note" paragraphs into blueprint `.tex` files.

## Read the other projects

They are in this workspace for a reason: the same lemma, pattern, or dead end has
often already been worked out next door. `"$HORIZON_BIN" search` spans **all**
projects — an existing construction in another project is a lead, whether you
import it, copy the approach, or read its blueprint. `references/` holds the
original sources (skill: `references`). Staying inside your own project because
the task named it is how the workspace re-derives the same thing three times.

## Delegating beyond your team (ask permission first)

Your normal way to parallelize is **within** your team: spawn subagents/workers
(skill: `subagents`) and dispatch scoped work to them in the foreground. That
needs no permission.

Launching work **outside** your team — creating new tasks for other teams, or

import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0RankOneNativePresentation

/-!
# The rank-one evaluation zero-locus comparison

The canonical inverse is cut out by the evaluation counit, while the existing divisor engine
consumes the tied cocycle datum's local equations.  This file proves the section-level comparison
between those two descriptions before any Noetherian or regularity hypothesis is introduced.

For a tied local presentation, transporting a datum section through `module_iso.inv` commutes
with restriction to every open.  Since every component of the sheaf isomorphism is injective,
restriction vanishes on the module side exactly when it vanishes on the datum side.  Applying
this to the canonical unit-lift through the evaluation counit identifies its restriction-
vanishing predicate with that of `datumSection`.  The final theorem specializes the comparison
to `PicRankOneNativePresentation`, whose converted module is definitionally the native module.

The second half passes to the canonical `O_X`-linear piece trivializations of the native module.
It proves that the evaluated section has coordinate `datum.component` on every cocycle piece, and
hence that the two principal local ideals agree.  This closes the local equation comparison, but
does not yet glue those ideals into a base-change-compatible family-level evaluation divisor.  The
file also does not assert regularity or manufacture the still-missing arbitrary-affine presentation
producer.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false
set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3

universe u

open CategoryTheory Limits TopologicalSpace Opposite MonoidalCategory
  CartesianMonoidalCategory

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
attribute [local instance 10000] relCurve.instOver

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
variable {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
variable {pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite pi]
variable {lam : picDegLayer C (genus C : ℤ) (overSpec k A)}

namespace BasicOpenCocycleDatum

variable {B : Type u} [CommRing B] [Algebra k B]

/-- The coordinate of a native global section on one cocycle piece.

This is obtained by restricting the section to `D.pieces j` and applying the canonical
`O_X`-linear trivialization of the native module there. -/
noncomputable def nativePieceCoordinate
    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B pi)
    (s : Γ(D.nativeModule, (⊤ : (relCurve C B).Opens)))
    (j : D.index) : Γ(relCurve C B, D.pieces j) :=
  gluedTriv B D.isGluingCocycle j le_rfl
    (gluedRes B D.pieces D.unit
      (le_top : D.pieces j ≤ (⊤ : (relCurve C B).Opens)) s)

/-- The native coordinate is the datum component of the same global section. -/
theorem nativePieceCoordinate_eq_component
    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B pi)
    (s : Γ(D.nativeModule, (⊤ : (relCurve C B).Opens)))
    (j : D.index) :
    D.nativePieceCoordinate s j = D.component s j := by
  rw [nativePieceCoordinate, gluedTriv_apply, gluedRes_coe]
  simp only [Scheme.resHom_resHom, component]

/-- Native piece coordinates commute with arbitrary affine coefficient extension. -/
theorem nativePieceCoordinate_sectionsMapTop
    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B pi)
    (B' : Type u) [CommRing B'] [Algebra k B'] [Algebra B B']
    [IsScalarTower k B B']
    (s : Γ(D.nativeModule, (⊤ : (relCurve C B).Opens)))
    (j : D.index) :
    (D.baseChange B').nativePieceCoordinate (D.sectionsMapTop B' s) j =
      D.toBasicOpenCoverData.piecesMap B' j (D.nativePieceCoordinate s j) := by
  rw [(D.baseChange B').nativePieceCoordinate_eq_component,
    D.component_sectionsMapTop B' s, D.nativePieceCoordinate_eq_component]

/-- The principal native-coordinate ideal is preserved by arbitrary affine coefficient
extension. This is the ideal-level consumer of `nativePieceCoordinate_sectionsMapTop`. -/
theorem nativePieceIdeal_sectionsMapTop
    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B pi)
    (B' : Type u) [CommRing B'] [Algebra k B'] [Algebra B B']
    [IsScalarTower k B B']
    (s : Γ(D.nativeModule, (⊤ : (relCurve C B).Opens)))
    (j : D.index) :
    Ideal.map (D.toBasicOpenCoverData.piecesMap B' j)
        (Ideal.span {D.nativePieceCoordinate s j}) =
      Ideal.span {
        (D.baseChange B').nativePieceCoordinate (D.sectionsMapTop B' s) j} := by
  rw [Ideal.map_span, Set.image_singleton, D.nativePieceCoordinate_sectionsMapTop]
  rfl

/-- The inverse of the native base-ring section equivalence is the identity on underlying
sections. -/
@[simp]
theorem nativeModuleKSectionsEquiv_symm_apply
    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B pi)
    (U : (relCurve C B).Opens) (s : D.sheaf.obj.obj (op U)) :
    (D.nativeModuleKSectionsEquiv U).symm s = s := by
  apply (D.nativeModuleKSectionsEquiv U).injective
  rw [LinearEquiv.apply_symm_apply]
  rfl

/-- The inverse component of the native base-ring sheaf isomorphism is the identity on
underlying sections. -/
@[simp]
theorem nativeModuleKSheafIso_inv_app
    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B pi)
    (U : (relCurve C B).Opens) (s : D.sheaf.obj.obj (op U)) :
    (D.nativeModuleKSheafIso.inv.hom.app (op U)).hom s = s := by
  change (D.nativeModuleKSectionsEquiv U).symm s = s
  exact D.nativeModuleKSectionsEquiv_symm_apply U s

end BasicOpenCocycleDatum

namespace PicRankOneLocalPresentation

/-- Transport through the tied sheaf isomorphism commutes with restriction on sections. -/
theorem module_iso_inv_restrict
    (P : PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam)
    {U V : (relCurve C P.cover.Carrier).Opens} (h : V ≤ U)
    (s : P.datum.sheaf.obj.obj (op U)) :
    (((Scheme.toModuleKSheafOfModules
      (Over.mk (relCurve C P.cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier)))
        P.module).obj.map (homOfLE h).op).hom
      ((P.module_iso.inv.hom.app (op U)).hom s)) =
      (P.module_iso.inv.hom.app (op V)).hom
        ((P.datum.sheaf.obj.map (homOfLE h).op).hom s) := by
  exact congrArg (fun z => z.hom s)
    (P.module_iso.inv.hom.naturality (homOfLE h).op).symm

/-- Restriction vanishes after transport to the base-ring module exactly when the datum restriction
vanishes.  This is a pointwise section comparison supplied by `module_iso`; it is not a statement
about the native `O_X`-module ideal and needs no Noetherian hypothesis. -/
theorem module_iso_inv_restrict_eq_zero_iff
    (P : PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam)
    {U V : (relCurve C P.cover.Carrier).Opens} (h : V ≤ U)
    (s : P.datum.sheaf.obj.obj (op U)) :
    (((Scheme.toModuleKSheafOfModules
      (Over.mk (relCurve C P.cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier)))
        P.module).obj.map (homOfLE h).op).hom
      ((P.module_iso.inv.hom.app (op U)).hom s) = 0) ↔
      ((P.datum.sheaf.obj.map (homOfLE h).op).hom s = 0) := by
  rw [P.module_iso_inv_restrict h s]
  exact map_eq_zero_iff _
    (CategoryTheory.ConcreteCategory.bijective_of_isIso
      (P.module_iso.inv.hom.app (op V))).1

/-- The evaluation counit sends the canonical H⁰ unit-lift to the module section obtained
from the tied datum class. -/
theorem evaluation_evaluationLiftOfH0_eq_moduleSectionsEquiv
    (P : PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam)
    (y : Sheaf.HModule P.datum.sheaf 0) :
    (Scheme.Modules.Hom.app P.evaluation
      ((relCurve C P.cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier)) ⁻¹ᵁ
        (⊤ : (Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier)).Opens))).hom
      (P.evaluationLiftOfH0 y) = P.moduleSectionsEquiv y := by
  calc
    _ = P.pushforwardSectionOfH0 y := P.evaluation_evaluationLiftOfH0 y
    _ = P.moduleSectionsEquiv y := rfl

/-- The canonical evaluation section and the tied datum section have the same restriction-
vanishing predicate on every open of the relative curve.

This is the immediate consumer of `module_iso_inv_restrict_eq_zero_iff`: the evaluated section
is first identified with `moduleSectionsEquiv y`, then with the inverse image of
`datumSection y` under the presentation's sheaf isomorphism. -/
theorem evaluationLift_restrict_eq_zero_iff
    (P : PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam)
    {V : (relCurve C P.cover.Carrier).Opens} (h : V ≤ ⊤)
    (y : Sheaf.HModule P.datum.sheaf 0) :
    (((Scheme.toModuleKSheafOfModules
      (Over.mk (relCurve C P.cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier)))
        P.module).obj.map (homOfLE h).op).hom
      ((Scheme.Modules.Hom.app P.evaluation
        ((relCurve C P.cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier)) ⁻¹ᵁ
          (⊤ : (Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier)).Opens))).hom
        (P.evaluationLiftOfH0 y)) = 0) ↔
      ((P.datum.sheaf.obj.map (homOfLE h).op).hom
        (P.datumSection y) = 0) := by
  rw [P.evaluation_evaluationLiftOfH0_eq_moduleSectionsEquiv y]
  rw [← P.module_iso_inv_datumSection y]
  exact P.module_iso_inv_restrict_eq_zero_iff h (P.datumSection y)

end PicRankOneLocalPresentation

namespace PicRankOneNativePresentation

/-- Native specialization of the evaluation/datum zero-locus comparison.

`toLocalPresentation.module` is definitionally `P.datum.nativeModule`, so this theorem is the
consumer-facing native base-ring section comparison rather than a second choice of line bundle.
The native `O_X`-linear ideal comparison remains a separate producer obligation. -/
theorem evaluationLift_restrict_eq_zero_iff
    (P : PicRankOneNativePresentation pi lam)
    {V : (relCurve C P.toLocalPresentation.cover.Carrier).Opens} (h : V ≤ ⊤)
    (y : Sheaf.HModule P.toLocalPresentation.datum.sheaf 0) :
    (((Scheme.toModuleKSheafOfModules
      (Over.mk (relCurve C P.toLocalPresentation.cover.Carrier ↘
        Spec (.of P.toLocalPresentation.cover.Carrier)))
        P.toLocalPresentation.module).obj.map (homOfLE h).op).hom
      ((Scheme.Modules.Hom.app P.toLocalPresentation.evaluation
        ((relCurve C P.toLocalPresentation.cover.Carrier ↘
          Spec (.of P.toLocalPresentation.cover.Carrier)) ⁻¹ᵁ
          (⊤ : (Spec (.of P.toLocalPresentation.cover.Carrier)).Opens))).hom
        (P.toLocalPresentation.evaluationLiftOfH0 y)) = 0) ↔
      ((P.toLocalPresentation.datum.sheaf.obj.map (homOfLE h).op).hom
        (P.toLocalPresentation.datumSection y) = 0) := by
  exact P.toLocalPresentation.evaluationLift_restrict_eq_zero_iff h y

/-- **Fibre nonvanishing of a datum section cutting a certified divisor**: if the local
equations cut by a germ-regular glued section of the datum are divisor-equal to a widened
locally certified system of degree `genus C`, then the compared section is nonzero on every
residue-field fibre of the base.

By contradiction: vanishing at `q` makes every pulled cut equation the zero section of the
fibre curve, while the certificate makes the pulled equations regular — and `0` is never a
nonzerodivisor in the nontrivial stalks of the integral fibre curve. -/
theorem sectionsMapTop_ne_zero_of_divEq_certified [IsAffineHom pi]
    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B pi)
    (s : ↥(gluedSubmodule B D.pieces D.unit ⊤))
    (𝒲 : (relCurve C B).PointedCover) (σ : relCurve C B → D.index)
    (hσ : ∀ x : relCurve C B, 𝒲.opens x ≤ D.pieces (σ x))
    (hreg : ∀ (j : D.index) (x : relCurve C B) (hx : x ∈ D.pieces j),
      ((relCurve C B).presheaf.germ (D.pieces j) x hx).hom (D.component s j)
        ∈ nonZeroDivisors ((relCurve C B).presheaf.stalk x))
    {d : (relCurve C B).LocalEquations}
    (hd : IsLocallyCertifiedAff (genus C) d)
    (hdiv : Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq (D.sectionLocalEquations s 𝒲 σ hσ hreg) d)
    (q : PrimeSpectrum B) :
    D.sectionsMapTop q.asIdeal.ResidueField s ≠ 0 := by
  intro hzero
  haveI : IsIntegral (relCurve C q.asIdeal.ResidueField) :=
    instIsIntegralBaseChange C q.asIdeal.ResidueField
  set e := D.sectionLocalEquations s 𝒲 σ hσ hreg with he
  set f := relCurveMap C B q.asIdeal.ResidueField with hf
  -- regularity of the pulled certified equations, transported across the `DivEq`

    f hdiv.symm (hd.germ_pullbackEqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors q.asIdeal.ResidueField (genus C))
  -- a point of the nonempty integral fibre curve

  have hz := hereg z z ((e.cover.pullback f).mem_opens z)

      (D.component s (σ (f.base z))) = 0 := by
    rw [← D.component_sectionsMapTop q.asIdeal.ResidueField s (σ (f.base z)), hzero,
      component_zero]

      (D.component s (σ (f.base z))) = 0 := by
    rw [← D.resHom_piecesMap_eq_relAffSectionsMap q.asIdeal.ResidueField (σ (f.base z))
      (D.component s (σ (f.base z))), hcomp0, map_zero]

    (le_rfl : f ⁻¹ᵁ D.pieces (σ (f.base z)) ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ D.pieces (σ (f.base z)))
    (le_rfl : f ⁻¹ᵁ 𝒲.opens (f.base z) ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ 𝒲.opens (f.base z))
    (Scheme.Hom.preimage_mono f (hσ (f.base z)))
    (D.component s (σ (f.base z)))

    calc Scheme.LocalEquations.pullbackEqn f e z
        = (relCurve C q.asIdeal.ResidueField).resHom
            (Scheme.Hom.preimage_mono f (hσ (f.base z)))
            (relAffSectionsMap C q.asIdeal.ResidueField (D.pieces (σ (f.base z)))
              (D.component s (σ (f.base z)))) := happ.symm
      _ = 0 := by rw [hval, map_zero]

`genus C` has nonzero image in every residue-field fibre `H⁰ ⊗ κ(q)` — exactly the

    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B pi)
    (hH1 : Subsingleton (datumPair D).H1)
    (y : Sheaf.HModule D.sheaf 0)
    (𝒲 : (relCurve C B).PointedCover) (σ : relCurve C B → D.index)
    (hσ : ∀ x : relCurve C B, 𝒲.opens x ≤ D.pieces (σ x))
    (hreg : ∀ (j : D.index) (x : relCurve C B) (hx : x ∈ D.pieces j),
      ((relCurve C B).presheaf.germ (D.pieces j) x hx).hom
        (D.component (Sheaf.HModule.linearEquiv₀
          (Opens.grothendieckTopology ((relCurve C B : Scheme.{u}) : TopCat))
          isTerminalTop D.sheaf y) j)

    (hd : IsLocallyCertifiedAff (genus C) d)

tied to that pullback.  This is the correct logical subfunctor underlying the future open Picard
locus; no openness or representability assertion is part of this definition. -/
def PicRankOneOpen :
    Subfunctor (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)) where
  obj T := {lam | ∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
      (t : overSpec k A ⟶ T.unop),

      ((picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).map t.op lam))}

    let F := picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)

      apply Subtype.ext

    (lam : (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).obj T) :

    94	/-- A represented genus divisor lies in the universal predicate exactly when its Abel image

    96	theorem divRankOneUniversalPredicate_mem_iff_sigma

   102	        (picRankOneOpenSigmaIncl pi).app (op T.unop.left) v =
   103	          (abelDivAffGenusSigma C).app (op T.unop.left) x.left := by
   104	  simp only [divRankOneUniversalPredicate,
   105	    divRankOnePresentationPreimageRepresenter,
   106	    Subfunctor.preimage_obj, Set.mem_preimage]
   107	  let p := (abelDivAffTrans C (genus C)).app T
   108	    ((divFunctorAff_genus_representableBy C).homEquiv x)
   109	  change p ∈ (PicRankOneOpen pi).obj T ↔ _
   110	  have hleft :
   111	      (abelDivAffGenusSigma C).app (op T.unop.left) x.left =
   112	        (⟨T.unop.hom, p⟩ :
   113	          (Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k))
   114	            (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ))).obj

   116	    abelDivAffGenusSigma_app_left_rankOne x

   118	  · intro hp
   119	    refine ⟨⟨T.unop.hom, ⟨p, hp⟩⟩, ?_⟩
   120	    rw [hleft]
   121	    rfl
   122	  · rintro ⟨v, hv⟩
   123	    rw [hleft] at hv
   124	    dsimp [picRankOneOpenSigmaIncl,

   127	    dsimp at hv
   128	    have hfirst : a = T.unop.hom :=

   133	        ConcreteCategory.hom

   161	    (x : (yoneda.obj D).obj T) :

   179	divisor rank-one open.  The carrier is the open image of the represented pullback of the Abel

   181	theorem divRankOneOpenData_of_picRankOneOpen_isOpen
   182	    (h : PicRankOneOpen.IsOpen pi) :
   183	    Nonempty (DivRankOneOpenData pi) := by
   184	  obtain ⟨X, snd, fst, hpb⟩ := h.rep (abelDivAffGenusSigma C)
   185	  letI : IsOpenImmersion snd :=
   186	    h.property (abelDivAffGenusSigma C) fst snd hpb

   189	  ext T x
   190	  rw [openSubfunctor_mem_iff]
   191	  rw [divRankOneUniversalPredicate_mem_iff_sigma]
   192	  have hpbT := (IsPullback.iff_app.mp hpb) (op T.unop.left)

   194	  constructor
   195	  · rintro ⟨y, hy⟩
   196	    have hxy : x.left = y.left ≫ U.ι := by
   197	      have hleft := congrArg Over.Hom.left hy
   198	      exact hleft.symm
   199	    have hrange : Set.range x.left.base ⊆ Set.range snd.base := by
   200	      rw [← Scheme.Hom.coe_opensRange snd]
   201	      rintro z ⟨t, rfl⟩
   202	      rw [hxy, Scheme.Hom.comp_apply]
   203	      change U.ι.base (y.left.base t) ∈ snd.opensRange
   204	      change U.ι.base (y.left.base t) ∈ U
   205	      exact (y.left.base t).property
   206	    let u : T.unop.left ⟶ X :=
   207	      IsOpenImmersion.lift snd x.left hrange
   208	    have hu : u ≫ snd = x.left :=
   209	      IsOpenImmersion.lift_fac _ _ _
   210	    refine ⟨fst.app (op T.unop.left) u, ?_⟩
   211	    have hcomm := congrArg
   212	      (fun f => (ConcreteCategory.hom f) u) hpbT.1
   213	    change (picRankOneOpenSigmaIncl pi).app (op T.unop.left)
   214	        (fst.app (op T.unop.left) u) =
   215	      (abelDivAffGenusSigma C).app (op T.unop.left) (u ≫ snd) at hcomm
   216	    simpa only [hu] using hcomm
   217	  · rintro ⟨v, hv⟩
   218	    obtain ⟨u, hu₁, hu₂⟩ := hpbT.2.2 v x.left hv
   219	    change u ≫ snd = x.left at hu₂
   220	    have hrange : Set.range x.left.base ⊆ Set.range U.ι.base := by
   221	      rw [Scheme.Opens.range_ι]
   222	      change Set.range x.left.base ⊆ snd.opensRange
   223	      rw [Scheme.Hom.coe_opensRange]
   224	      rintro z ⟨t, rfl⟩
   225	      refine ⟨u.base t, ?_⟩
   226	      have happ := congrArg (fun f => f.base t) hu₂
   227	      simpa only [Scheme.Hom.comp_apply] using happ
   228	    let V : Over (Spec (.of k)) :=
   229	      Over.mk (U.ι ≫ (divRepAffGenusScheme C).hom)
   230	    let j : V ⟶ divRepAffGenusScheme C :=
   231	      Over.homMk (U := V) U.ι
   232	    let e : U.toScheme = V.left := rfl
   233	    let l : T.unop.left ⟶ U.toScheme :=
   234	      IsOpenImmersion.lift U.ι x.left hrange
   235	    let l' : T.unop.left ⟶ V.left := l ≫ eqToHom e
   236	    have he : eqToHom e ≫ j.left = U.ι := by
   237	      subst e
   238	      rfl
   239	    have hl : l' ≫ j.left = x.left := by
   240	      dsimp only [l']
   241	      rw [Category.assoc, he]
   242	      dsimp only [l]
   243	      exact IsOpenImmersion.lift_fac _ _ _
   244	    have hlw : l' ≫ V.hom = T.unop.hom := by
   245	      rw [← j.w, ← Category.assoc, hl]
   246	      exact x.w
   247	    let y : (yoneda.obj V).obj T := Over.homMk l' hlw
   248	    refine ⟨y, ?_⟩
   249	    change y ≫ j = x
   250	    apply Over.OverMorphism.ext
   251	    exact hl

    84	    (mu : pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k K)) :
    85	    ∃ (L : Type u) (_ : Field L) (_ : Algebra k L) (_ : Algebra K L)
    86	        (_ : IsScalarTower k K L) (_ : Module.Finite K L)
    87	        (_ : Algebra.IsSeparable K L)

    89	        (r : SepClosedTranslatedDropResult (C := C) (L := L) mu.1 d),
    90	      classDeg k (chartTwistClass C d.m r.Z) = (genus C : Int) ∧
    91	        (Set.Finite (r.S.support : Set {x : (C ⊗ overSpec k L).left //

    93	          (∀ p : {x : (C ⊗ overSpec k L).left //
    94	              x ≠ genericPoint (C ⊗ overSpec k L).left},

    27	/-- For the pullback pseudofunctor of over categories, `pullHom` is the literal
    28	three-factor pullback comparison. -/
    29	lemma pullHom_eq_pullbackFaceIsoOfEq_hom
    30	    {D : Type u} [Category.{v, u} D] [HasPullbacks D]
    31	    {V W X : D} (r₀ r₁ : V ⟶ X) (q : V ⟶ W) (p₀ p₁ : W ⟶ X)
    32	    (J : Over X) (h₀ : r₀ = q ≫ p₀) (h₁ : r₁ = q ≫ p₁)
    33	    (i : (Over.pullback p₀).obj J ≅ (Over.pullback p₁).obj J) :
    34	    pullHom (F := Over.pullbackPseudofunctor (C := D)) i.hom q r₀ r₁ h₀.symm h₁.symm =
    35	      (Functor.RepresentableBy.Over.pullbackFaceIsoOfEq
    36	        r₀ r₁ q p₀ p₁ h₀ h₁ i).hom := by
    37	  subst r₀
    38	  subst r₁
    39	  rfl

    10	/-!
    11	# Affine etale descent for Pic0
    12	
    13	Compatible degree-zero Picard data over a singleton faithfully flat etale cover descend
    14	uniquely to the affine base.  Existence first descends the underlying `PicEtAff` class, then
    15	reflects the fibrewise degree-zero condition through the cover.  Uniqueness is affine
    16	`PicEtAff` etale separatedness.
    17	
    18	This is the affine algebraic input for the big-etale sheaf comparison.  It does not assert a
    19	Scheme-site sheaf certificate or identify the raw functor with its sheafification.
    20	-/
    21	
    22	set_option autoImplicit false
    23	
    24	universe u
    25	
    26	open CategoryTheory
    27	
    28	open scoped TensorProduct
    29	
    30	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    31	
    32	noncomputable section
    33	
    34	/-- Compatible degree-zero Picard data over a singleton faithfully flat etale cover have a
    35	unique degree-zero descent to the affine base. -/
    36	theorem pic0Subgroup_existsUnique_of_etaleCover
    37	    {k A : Type u} [Field k] [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    38	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom]
    39	    [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    40	    [GeometricallyReduced C.hom]
    41	    (E : Algebra.EtaleCover A)
    42	    (x : pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k E.Carrier))
    43	    (h : pic0Map C (Over.overSpecMap (doubleInl E)) x =
    44	      pic0Map C (Over.overSpecMap (doubleInr E)) x) :
    45	    ∃! z : pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k A),
    46	      pic0Map C
    47	        (Over.overSpecMap
    48	          ((Algebra.ofId A E.Carrier).restrictScalars k)) z = x := by
    49	  let phi : A →ₐ[k] E.Carrier :=
    50	    (Algebra.ofId A E.Carrier).restrictScalars k
    51	  have hPic :
    52	      picEtMap C (Over.overSpecMap (doubleInl E))
    53	          (x : picEt C (overSpec k E.Carrier)) =
    54	        picEtMap C (Over.overSpecMap (doubleInr E))
    55	          (x : picEt C (overSpec k E.Carrier)) := by
    56	    exact congrArg Subtype.val h
    57	  have hAff :
    58	      PicEtAff.mapAlg C (doubleInl E)
    59	          (picEtAffineEquiv C E.Carrier
    60	            (x : picEt C (overSpec k E.Carrier))) =
    61	        PicEtAff.mapAlg C (doubleInr E)
    62	          (picEtAffineEquiv C E.Carrier
    63	            (x : picEt C (overSpec k E.Carrier))) := by
    64	    rw [← picEtAffineEquiv_naturality, ← picEtAffineEquiv_naturality]
    65	    exact congrArg (picEtAffineEquiv C (E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier)) hPic
    66	  obtain ⟨zAff, hzAff⟩ :=
    67	    PicEtAff.exists_map_eq_of_double_eq C E
    68	      (picEtAffineEquiv C E.Carrier
    69	        (x : picEt C (overSpec k E.Carrier))) hAff
    70	  let zPic : picEt C (overSpec k A) :=
    71	    (picEtAffineEquiv C A).symm zAff
    72	  have hzPic :
    73	      picEtMap C (Over.overSpecMap phi) zPic =
    74	        (x : picEt C (overSpec k E.Carrier)) := by
    75	    apply (picEtAffineEquiv C E.Carrier).injective
    76	    rw [picEtAffineEquiv_naturality]
    77	    simp only [zPic, MulEquiv.apply_symm_apply]
    78	    rw [PicEtAff.mapAlg_eq_map_of_toRingHom_eq_algebraMap C phi rfl]
    79	    exact hzAff
    80	  have hzMem : zPic ∈ pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k A) :=
    81	    mem_pic0Subgroup_of_etaleCover E zPic (by
    82	      rw [hzPic]
    83	      exact x.2)
    84	  let z : pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k A) := ⟨zPic, hzMem⟩
    85	  have hz :
    86	      pic0Map C
    87	        (Over.overSpecMap
    88	          ((Algebra.ofId A E.Carrier).restrictScalars k)) z = x :=
    89	    Subtype.ext hzPic
    90	  refine ⟨z, hz, ?_⟩
    91	  intro y hy
    92	  apply Subtype.ext
    93	  apply (picEtAffineEquiv C A).injective
    94	  apply PicEtAff.map_injective_of_etaleCover C E
    95	  have hyz := hy.trans hz.symm
    96	  have hyPic :
    97	      picEtMap C (Over.overSpecMap phi)
    98	          (y : picEt C (overSpec k A)) =
    99	        picEtMap C (Over.overSpecMap phi)
   100	          (z : picEt C (overSpec k A)) := by
   101	    exact congrArg Subtype.val hyz
   102	  have hyAff := congrArg (picEtAffineEquiv C E.Carrier) hyPic
   103	  rw [picEtAffineEquiv_naturality, picEtAffineEquiv_naturality,
   104	    PicEtAff.mapAlg_eq_map_of_toRingHom_eq_algebraMap C phi rfl,
   105	    PicEtAff.mapAlg_eq_map_of_toRingHom_eq_algebraMap C phi rfl] at hyAff
   106	  exact hyAff
   107	
   108	end
   109	
   110	end AlgebraicGeometry

     6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0RankOneLocalDivisor
     7	
     8	/-!
     9	# Affine evaluation-divisor coherence for the FibrePresented producer
    10	
    11	The arbitrary-scheme `PicRankOneOpen.FibrePresented` producer needs a divisor cut by the
    12	canonical evaluation section which is stable under restriction of affine test schemes.  This
    13	file records two construction-level inputs for that gluing step:
    14	
    15	* `datumSectionBaseChange_tower` proves that the tied datum section itself is coherent along
    16	  every affine coefficient tower;
    17	* `baseOpenRankOneDivisor_mul_eq` proves independence of the chosen rank-one generator after
    18	  passing to a pairwise product open.
    19	
    20	The remaining gluing edge is deliberately explicit: one must identify `DivFamZarAff.mapAlg` of
    21	the local divisor with the divisor cut by the tower-transported section.  No
    22	`PicRankOneOpen.FibrePresented` or pullback-square hypothesis is introduced here.
    23	-/
    24	
    25	set_option autoImplicit false
    26	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false
    27	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
    28	
    29	universe u
    30	
    31	open CategoryTheory Limits TopologicalSpace Opposite
    32	open scoped TensorProduct
    33	
    34	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    35	
    36	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
    37	
    38	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    39	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    40	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    41	variable {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    42	variable {pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite pi]
    43	variable {lam : picDegLayer C (genus C : ℤ) (overSpec k A)}
    44	
    45	namespace PicRankOneLocalPresentation
    46	
    47	/-- The actual section attached to a tied presentation is transitive under arbitrary affine
    48	coefficient extension.  The cast is along the canonical equality between iterated and direct
    49	base change of the same cocycle datum. -/
    50	theorem datumSectionBaseChange_tower
    51	    (P : PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam)
    52	    (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [Algebra k B] [Algebra P.cover.Carrier B]
    53	    [IsScalarTower k P.cover.Carrier B]
    54	    (B' : Type u) [CommRing B'] [Algebra k B'] [Algebra P.cover.Carrier B']
    55	    [Algebra B B'] [IsScalarTower k P.cover.Carrier B'] [IsScalarTower k B B']
    56	    [IsScalarTower P.cover.Carrier B B']
    57	    (y : Sheaf.HModule P.datum.sheaf 0) :
    58	    let hD : (P.datum.baseChange B).baseChange B' = P.datum.baseChange B' :=
    59	      P.datum.baseChange_baseChange C P.cover.Carrier B B'
    60	    cast (congrArg (fun E : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B' pi =>
    61	      ↑(gluedSubmodule B' E.pieces E.unit ⊤)) hD)
    62	        ((P.datum.baseChange B).sectionsMapTop B'
    63	          (P.datumSectionBaseChange B y)) =
    64	      P.datumSectionBaseChange B' y := by
    65	  rw [P.datumSectionBaseChange_one_tmul B y,
    66	    P.datumSectionBaseChange_one_tmul B' y]
    67	  exact P.datum.sectionsMapTop_tower
    68	    C P.cover.Carrier B B' (P.datumSection y)
    69	
    70	/-- A generator which is fibrewise nonzero on `D(f)` remains so on `D(f * g)`. -/
    71	theorem generator_nonzero_on_mul_left
    72	    (P : PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam)
    73	    (f g : P.cover.Carrier)
    74	    (y : Sheaf.HModule P.datum.sheaf 0)
    75	    (hy : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum P.cover.Carrier, f ∉ p.asIdeal →
    76	      (y ⊗ₜ (1 : p.asIdeal.ResidueField) :
    77	        Sheaf.HModule P.datum.sheaf 0 ⊗[P.cover.Carrier]
    78	          p.asIdeal.ResidueField) ≠ 0) :
    79	    ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum P.cover.Carrier, f * g ∉ p.asIdeal →
    80	      (y ⊗ₜ (1 : p.asIdeal.ResidueField) :
    81	        Sheaf.HModule P.datum.sheaf 0 ⊗[P.cover.Carrier]
    82	          p.asIdeal.ResidueField) ≠ 0 := by
    83	  intro p hfg
    84	  exact hy p fun hf => hfg (p.asIdeal.mul_mem_right g hf)
    85	
    86	/-- A generator which is fibrewise nonzero on `D(g)` remains so on `D(f * g)`. -/
    87	theorem generator_nonzero_on_mul_right
    88	    (P : PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam)
    89	    (f g : P.cover.Carrier)
    90	    (y : Sheaf.HModule P.datum.sheaf 0)
    91	    (hy : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum P.cover.Carrier, g ∉ p.asIdeal →
    92	      (y ⊗ₜ (1 : p.asIdeal.ResidueField) :
    93	        Sheaf.HModule P.datum.sheaf 0 ⊗[P.cover.Carrier]
    94	          p.asIdeal.ResidueField) ≠ 0) :
    95	    ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum P.cover.Carrier, f * g ∉ p.asIdeal →
    96	      (y ⊗ₜ (1 : p.asIdeal.ResidueField) :
    97	        Sheaf.HModule P.datum.sheaf 0 ⊗[P.cover.Carrier]
    98	          p.asIdeal.ResidueField) ≠ 0 := by
    99	  intro p hfg
   100	  exact hy p fun hg => hfg (p.asIdeal.mul_mem_left f hg)
   101	
   102	/-- Local evaluation divisors cut by two rank-one generators agree on the direct pairwise
   103	product open.  This is the generator-independence half of the compatibility premise required
   104	by `divFamZarAff.exists_glue_of_basic_compat`. -/
   105	theorem baseOpenRankOneDivisor_mul_eq
   106	    (P : PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam)
   107	    [IsNoetherianRing P.cover.Carrier]
   108	    (f g : P.cover.Carrier)
   109	    (y y' : Sheaf.HModule P.datum.sheaf 0)
   110	    (hy : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum P.cover.Carrier, f ∉ p.asIdeal →
   111	      (y ⊗ₜ (1 : p.asIdeal.ResidueField) :
   112	        Sheaf.HModule P.datum.sheaf 0 ⊗[P.cover.Carrier]
   113	          p.asIdeal.ResidueField) ≠ 0)
   114	    (hy' : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum P.cover.Carrier, g ∉ p.asIdeal →
   115	      (y' ⊗ₜ (1 : p.asIdeal.ResidueField) :
   116	        Sheaf.HModule P.datum.sheaf 0 ⊗[P.cover.Carrier]
   117	          p.asIdeal.ResidueField) ≠ 0) :
   118	    P.baseOpenRankOneDivisor (f * g) y
   119	        (P.generator_nonzero_on_mul_left f g y hy) =
   120	      P.baseOpenRankOneDivisor (f * g) y'
   121	        (P.generator_nonzero_on_mul_right f g y' hy') :=
   122	  P.baseOpenRankOneDivisor_eq (f * g) y y'
   123	    (P.generator_nonzero_on_mul_left f g y hy)
   124	    (P.generator_nonzero_on_mul_right f g y' hy')
   125	
   126	end PicRankOneLocalPresentation
   127	
   128	end AlgebraicGeometry

/-- Expose a supplied relative-open certificate without hiding it behind typeclass search. -/
theorem picRankOneOpen_isOpen_of_certificate
    (h : PicRankOneOpen.IsOpen pi) : PicRankOneOpen.IsOpen pi :=
  h

/-- Extract the open immersion supplied by the relative-openness certificate on an arbitrary
pullback.  This is the exact shape consumed by an eventual chart/fibre producer. -/
theorem picRankOneOpen_openPullback
    (h : PicRankOneOpen.IsOpen pi)
    {X Z : Scheme.{u}}
    (g : yoneda.obj X ⟶
      Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)))
    (fst : yoneda.obj Z ⟶
      Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (PicRankOneOpen pi).toFunctor)
    (snd : Z ⟶ X)
    (hpb : IsPullback fst (yoneda.map snd) (picRankOneOpenSigmaIncl pi) g) :
    IsOpenImmersion snd :=
  h.property g fst snd hpb

/-- Pullback stability of the public rank-one locus, exposed independently of its definition. -/
theorem picRankOneOpen_map_mem {T T' : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
    (f : T ⟶ T') {lam : (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).obj T}
    (h : lam ∈ (PicRankOneOpen pi).obj T) :
    (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).map f lam ∈ (PicRankOneOpen pi).obj T' :=
  (PicRankOneOpen pi).map f h

/-- Pullback stability of the public locus, with the base-change direction made explicit. -/

    (f : T ⟶ T') {lam : (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).obj T}
    (h : lam ∈ (PicRankOneOpen pi).obj T) :
    (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).map f lam ∈ (PicRankOneOpen pi).obj T' :=

This name deliberately records only a presentation-theoretic preimage.  It is not the future

    (divRankOnePresentationPreimageRepresenter pi).toFunctor ⟶
      (PicRankOneOpen pi).toFunctor :=
  rankOneRepresenterRestriction pi ≫ rankOneAbelAff pi

/-- Immediate consumer theorem: the restricted represented Abel map lands in the public locus.
The stronger canonical inverse still needs the family-level divisor/evaluation producer; this
theorem records the exact target API that consumer lanes can use today. -/
theorem rankOneAbelRepresented_mem {T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
    (x : (divRankOnePresentationPreimageRepresenter pi).obj T) :
    ((rankOneAbelRepresented pi).app T x :
      (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)).obj T) ∈ (PicRankOneOpen pi).obj T :=
  ((rankOneAbelRepresented pi).app T x).property

end

    12	
    13	/-! # The Jacobian of a smooth proper curve
    14	
    15	The Jacobian of a smooth, proper, geometrically irreducible curve over a field, equipped with
    16	its structure as an abelian variety.
    17	
    18	## Status
    19	
    20	The Jacobian is defined uniformly as the underlying scheme of an Albanese witness
    21	(`JacobianWitness`) for the curve `C`; the four protected instances on `Jacobian C` all
    22	project from the witness directly.
    23	
    24	The construction is **uniform in the genus**: the witness is the Picard identity
    25	component `Pic⁰_{C/k}` (`picardJacobianWitness`), an abelian variety of dimension
    26	`genus C` built by the FGA route (`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.*` +
    27	`AlgebraicJacobian.Albanese.*`). There is **no** genus `= 0` / genus `> 0` split: when
    28	`genus C = 0` the tangent space `H¹(C, 𝒪_C)` is `0`-dimensional, so `Pic⁰_{C/k} = Spec k`
    29	falls out automatically. The former separate `genusZeroWitness` lane (with its
    30	`RigidityKbar` / cotangent-vanishing / Frobenius / `ℙ¹`-identification machinery) was a
    31	pre-FGA local optimisation and has been removed.
    32	
    33	`picardJacobianWitness` is wired to the `Pic⁰_{C/k}` development in its **étale** form
    34	(`Picard/Pic0Et.lean`): the witness scheme is `Scheme.Pic0SchemeEt C`, the identity
    35	component of the scheme representing the *étale-sheafified* relative Picard functor. It
    36	carries **no hypothesis on `C(k)`** — exactly the three challenge hypotheses and nothing
    37	else — which is the owner decision of 2026-07-28 (protection I-0491) and the full strength
    38	the challenge asks for.
    39	
    40	Why sheafifying is what makes that possible. Over an arbitrary field one cannot ask for
    41	representability of the *unsheafified* functor `T ↦ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)`
    42	(`picSharp`): Kleiman L5105–L5108 exhibits the conic `u² + v² + w² = 0` in `ℙ²_ℝ` — a
    43	smooth plane conic, hence smooth, proper and geometrically integral, over a field where it
    44	has no rational point — for which he concludes `Pic_{X/ℝ}` is not representable while
    45	`Pic_{(X/ℝ)ét}` is. The étale sheafification is Kleiman's own object; its sheaf property is
    46	*proved* in `Picard/PicEtSheaf.lean` (`picEt_isSheaf_forget`), not assumed.
    47	
    48	**Two corrections to what this paragraph used to say** (`review-ajc`, 2026-07-30), both of
    49	which had already been made at the seam and in the blueprint and were missed *here*, in the
    50	file a reader opens first.
    51	
    52	*The reason was wrong.* This said `picSharp` "is not a sheaf even Zariski-locally". No
    53	source supports that for the **relative** functor: the lines it came from
    54	(Kleiman §2 L1292–L1302) are about the **absolute** `Pic_X`, and `picSharp` is *defined* by
    55	quotienting out `Pic(T)` precisely to defeat that argument. Kleiman's own claim about the
    56	relative functor is the much weaker "not *a priori* a sheaf" (L1330), and `th:cmp` part 1
    57	points the other way — `Pic_{X/S}` *injects* into `Pic_{(X/S)zar}` whenever
    58	`O_S = f_*O_X` universally, automatic on these binders, so **in Kleiman** `picSharp` is
    59	Zariski-*separated* here.
    60	
    61	That last sentence is a statement about the SOURCE, and the Lean citation I first attached
    62	to it does not carry it (`review-ajc`, corrected in the same session by a fresh-context
    63	audit of my own fix). `PicScheme.picSharp_isSheaf_zariski_of_representableBy`
    64	(`Picard/PicEtSubcanonical.lean`) takes a `rep : (picSharp C).RepresentableBy X`
    65	hypothesis: it says a *representable* `picSharp` is a Zariski sheaf, by subcanonicity —
    66	which is the converse direction and is conditional on the thing the seam does not have.
    67	`PicEtSubcanonical`'s own §4 docstring scopes it correctly as "only the first half"; that
    68	caveat is what I dropped when I copied the citation here. Nothing in this project proves
    69	`th:cmp` part 1. Do not restore a Zariski-sheaf reason in this slot; two replacement
    70	citations have already been wrong in it (`I-0970`, `I-0973`), and this was a third.
    71	
    72	*And "**false**" overstates what is proved.* The non-representability of `picSharp` is a
    73	Lean theorem only *conditionally*:
    74	`PicScheme.not_exists_representing_picSharp_of_not_isIso`
    75	(`Picard/PicEtSubcanonical.lean`) derives from `¬ IsIso (picEtComparison C)` that no scheme
    76	represents `picSharp C`. Its antecedent — that the comparison genuinely fails for that conic
    77	— is **quoted from Kleiman, not formalised here**; doing so means exhibiting `φ^*O(1)` in
    78	`picEt C (Spec ℝ)` outside the image via `h⁰` on `ℙ¹_ℂ`. So the accurate word for the
    79	unsheafified statement over arbitrary `k` is **unproved with a refutation route mapped
    80	out**, not "false". `Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean` says exactly this at
    81	`fgaPicardRepresentability`, and says that writing "FALSE" here is the error the board row
    82	was corrected for in the opposite direction.
    83	
    84	## The five obligations, and none of them is false
    85	
    86	Be precise about what the wiring buys, because "invoked upstream" is not "proved
    87	upstream". The witness reaches **five** open obligations:
    88	
    89	1. `Scheme.fgaPicardRepresentability` — representability of the étale-sheafified functor
    90	   over an arbitrary field (`Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean`). The project's central
    91	   open obligation, expected to stay open;
    92	2. `Scheme.Pic0Et.geometricallyReduced` — Cartier's theorem in characteristic zero, a
    93	   genuine statement in characteristic `p`;
    94	3. `Scheme.Pic0Et.universallyClosed` — Kleiman §5 Thm. `th:qpp&p`;
    95	4. `smoothOfRelativeDimension_genus_pic0Et`, 5. `isAlbanese_pic0Et` — the two leaves
    96	   stated below, each at exactly the strength the assembly consumes.
    97	
    98	Note (2) and (3) rather than smoothness and properness: `Pic0Et.smooth` and
    99	`Pic0Et.proper` are **assemblies** over them, not obligations of their own, and citing
   100	them as the open statements is a stale reading. What *is* proved unconditionally, and
   101	measures axiom-clean: `Pic0Et.grpObj`, `Pic0Et.geometricallyIrreducible`,
   102	`Pic0Et.locallyOfFiniteType`, `Pic0Et.isSeparated`.
   103	
   104	**The five are NOT independent, and the list must not be read as five distances to be
   105	added** — measured 2026-07-29 r2 (`ajc-p2`, `Picard/Pic0EtRelativeDimension.lean`;
   106	independently reproduced by `ajc-p3`). Obligation 4 **implies** obligation 2: leaf B gives
   107	bare smoothness by `SmoothOfRelativeDimension.smooth` and then geometric reducedness by
   108	this project's `Smooth.geometricallyReduced`, packaged as
   109	`Scheme.Pic0Et.geometricallyReduced_of_leafB`. So closing leaf B would close two of the
   110	five at once, and obligation 2 is a *sub-problem* of obligation 4 rather than a peer of
   111	it. What does **not** follow is that obligation 2 became cheaper: it is the weaker
   112	statement, so proving it directly (the `k̄` reduction on `AJC.pic0av.structure`) remains
   113	the right attack, and the implication is useless in that direction. The other three are
   114	mutually independent as far as anything measured shows.
   115	
   116	**All five are true statements awaiting proofs**, and that is the substance of the 2026-07-28
   117	change rather than the count. The former leaf `hasRationalPoint_of_curve` asserted a
   118	`k`-rational point from the challenge hypotheses alone; it was *false*, so the witness rested
   119	on an inconsistent hypothesis and its consequences were vacuously true — a state no axiom
   120	check can distinguish from an honest one. It has been deleted, never proved. The count was
   121	five before and is five now; what changed is that no obligation is a false statement any
   122	more.
   123	
   124	That the headline carries no rational-point binder is **checked**, not asserted: the
   125	`HeadlineBinders` section of `scripts/axiom-frontier.lean` elaborates every headline
   126	declaration under exactly the three challenge hypotheses and stops compiling if a
   127	`[HasRationalPoint _]` binder ever returns.
   128	
   129	Two conditional results are kept beside the headline and **neither may be presented as
   130	it**: `picardJacobianWitnessOfHasRationalPoint`, the same assembly on the *unsheafified*
   131	functor with `C(k) ≠ ∅` as a hypothesis (true, strictly weaker than the challenge), and
   132	`picardJacobianWitnessOfIsAlgClosed`, a genuine theorem over `k̄`. Their gate
   133	`Scheme.HasPicScheme` has no instance: its only producer is the named theorem
   134	`Scheme.picSchemeOfHasRationalPoint`, so nothing acquires a rational point by synthesis.
   135	
   136	The two étale leaves are each stated at exactly the strength the assembly consumes, and
   137	each carries a *companion* measuring what the landed development already reaches, so the
   138	remaining distance is compiler-checked rather than described:
   139	
   140	- `smoothOfRelativeDimension_genus_pic0Et` — bare smoothness of `Pic⁰_{C/k}` refined to
   141	  relative dimension `genus C`. `finrank_tangentSpace_pic0_eq_genus` measures what remains:
   142	  the leaf owes a translation between two invariants of smoothness — the tangent-space
   143	  dimension and the rank of `Ω`, which is what Mathlib's presentation-based
   144	  `SmoothOfRelativeDimension` is characterised by. Two corrections to what this entry used
   145	  to say, both from the 2026-07-29 pass (`ajc-p2`, `I-0975`): the dimension count is *not*
   146	  "landed mathematics" — `Pic0.finrank_cotangentSpace_eq_finrank_hModuleOne` reports
   147	  `sorryAx`; and there is no "transport of that landed chain from `Pic0Scheme` to
   148	  `Pic0SchemeEt`" to pay for, because the chain **restates** at the étale object with no
   149	  comparison of the two Picard schemes (`Picard/Pic0EtTangentSpace.lean`). The étale
   150	  formulation's own dimension count is proved there from a single named antecedent.
   151	- `isAlbanese_pic0Et` — the Albanese universal property over an arbitrary base field and
   152	  for every marked point, where the landed proof covers the algebraically closed,
   153	  positive-genus case. `isAlbanese_pic0_of_isAlgClosed` measures the distance exactly:
   154	  in that case the universal property *is* the landed
   155	  `Albanese.Pic0.albanese_universal_property` with no transport, and what the leaf adds
   156	  is arbitrary base field, genus `0`, and the basepoint condition `P ≫ ι_P = η`.
   157	
   158	The `picSharp`-shaped leaves `smoothOfRelativeDimension_genus_pic0` and `isAlbanese_pic0`
   159	are retained below: they are the obligations of the *conditional* milestone
   160	`picardJacobianWitnessOfHasRationalPoint`, not of the headline.
   161	
   162	The file contains:
   163	- `IsAlbanese`: the Albanese universal property for a pointed curve.
   164	- `IsAlbanese.unique`: uniqueness of the Albanese object up to canonical isomorphism.
   165	- `JacobianWitness`: a bundled candidate Albanese object together with the universal
   166	  property uniformly over the choice of $k$-rational marked point.
   167	- `geometricallyIntegral_of_curve`: the Picard development's `GeometricallyIntegral`
   168	  hypothesis, derived from the challenge hypotheses.
   169	- `finrank_tangentSpace_pic0_eq_genus` and `isAlbanese_pic0_of_isAlgClosed`: the parts of
   170	  leaves B and C that the landed development already proves, stated at the headline so
   171	  that each leaf's remaining distance is compiler-checked rather than described.
   172	- `hasRationalPoint_of_curve_of_isAlgClosed` and `picardJacobianWitnessOfIsAlgClosed`:
   173	  leaf A discharged over an algebraically closed field, and the witness assembled without
   174	  the inconsistent leaf. Unlike the two companions above the first of these is axiom-clean
   175	  and is a discharge rather than a record of distance.
   176	- `picardJacobianWitnessOfHasRationalPoint`: the assembly itself, with the rational point
   177	  as a hypothesis rather than a source. Both witnesses below are `haveI` specialisations of
   178	  it, so neither repeats a field, and it is the compiled form of branch (1) of the open
   179	  decision — a headline carrying `C(k) ≠ ∅` needs no new mathematics beyond this. Branch
   180	  (2) is not reachable from it; see its docstring.
   181	- the four leaves above — two in the `picSharp` shape, two in the étale shape — and
   182	  `picardJacobianWitness`, the Albanese witness `J = Pic⁰_{C/k}` assembled from the
   183	  étale pair with no `sorry` of its own.
   184	- `nonempty_jacobianWitness`: existence of an Albanese witness for every curve,
   185	  delegating to `picardJacobianWitness`.
   186	- `Jacobian` and its four protected instances, each obtained by projection from the
   187	  Albanese witness.
   188	
   189	### Forbidden shortcut (sanity check)
   190	
   191	Defining `Jacobian C := 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k)))` *unconditionally* (the terminal object,
   192	i.e. `Spec k`) compiles and discharges three of the four instances for free, but the
   193	fourth instance `SmoothOfRelativeDimension (genus C) (𝟙_ _).hom` would force `genus C = 0`,
   194	which is mathematically wrong for any curve of genus `≥ 1`. The terminal-object definition
   195	is therefore forbidden when `genus C > 0`. The witness-based definition avoids this
   196	issue: the witness's `J` is `Pic⁰_{C/k}`, which is `Spec k` exactly when `genus C = 0`
   197	and the honest Albanese object otherwise.
   198	-/
   199	
   200	set_option autoImplicit false
   201	
   202	universe u
   203	
   204	open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory MonObj
   205	
   206	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
   207	
   208	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
   209	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom]
   210	  [IsProper C.hom]
   211	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
   212	
   213	/-- The Albanese universal property for a pointed smooth proper curve `(C, P)`.
   214	An object `J` (with abelian-variety structure) is the Albanese of `(C, P)` if it
   215	receives a universal pointed morphism `C ⟶ J` sending `P` to the identity. -/
   216	def IsAlbanese (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) (P : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ C)
   217	    (J : Over (Spec (.of k)))
   218	    [GrpObj J] [IsProper J.hom] [Smooth J.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible J.hom] : Prop :=
   219	  ∃ α : C ⟶ J, P ≫ α = η[J] ∧
   220	    ∀ {A : Over (Spec (.of k))} [GrpObj A] [IsProper A.hom]
   221	      [Smooth A.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible A.hom] (f : C ⟶ A) (_ : P ≫ f = η[A]),
   222	      ∃! (g : J ⟶ A), f = α ≫ g
   223	
   224	namespace IsAlbanese
   225	
   226	noncomputable def ofCurve {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
   227	    {P : 𝟙_ _ ⟶ C} {J : Over (Spec (.of k))} [GrpObj J] [IsProper J.hom] [Smooth J.hom]
   228	    [GeometricallyIrreducible J.hom] (h : IsAlbanese C P J) : C ⟶ J :=
   229	  Classical.choose h
   230	
   231	lemma comp_ofCurve {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
   232	    {P : 𝟙_ _ ⟶ C} {J : Over (Spec (.of k))} [GrpObj J] [IsProper J.hom] [Smooth J.hom]
   233	    [GeometricallyIrreducible J.hom] (h : IsAlbanese C P J) :
   234	    P ≫ h.ofCurve = η[J] :=
   235	  (Classical.choose_spec h).1
   236	
   237	lemma exists_unique_ofCurve_comp {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
   238	    {P : 𝟙_ _ ⟶ C} {J : Over (Spec (.of k))} [GrpObj J] [IsProper J.hom] [Smooth J.hom]
   239	    [GeometricallyIrreducible J.hom] (h : IsAlbanese C P J)
   240	    {A : Over (Spec (.of k))} [GrpObj A] [IsProper A.hom] [Smooth A.hom]
   241	    [GeometricallyIrreducible A.hom] (f : C ⟶ A) (hf : P ≫ f = η[A]) :
   242	    ∃! (g : J ⟶ A), f = h.ofCurve ≫ g :=
   243	  (Classical.choose_spec h).2 f hf
   244	
   245	/-- The Albanese object is unique up to a unique isomorphism compatible with the
   246	universal morphisms. -/
   247	theorem unique {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))} {P : 𝟙_ _ ⟶ C}
   248	    {J₁ J₂ : Over (Spec (.of k))}
   249	    [GrpObj J₁] [IsProper J₁.hom] [Smooth J₁.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible J₁.hom]
   250	    [GrpObj J₂] [IsProper J₂.hom] [Smooth J₂.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible J₂.hom]
   251	    (h₁ : IsAlbanese C P J₁) (h₂ : IsAlbanese C P J₂) :
   252	    ∃! (e : J₁ ⟶ J₂), h₂.ofCurve = h₁.ofCurve ≫ e := by
   253	  have ⟨g, hg_eq, hg_unique⟩ := h₁.exists_unique_ofCurve_comp h₂.ofCurve h₂.comp_ofCurve
   254	  have ⟨h, hh_eq, hh_unique⟩ := h₂.exists_unique_ofCurve_comp h₁.ofCurve h₁.comp_ofCurve
   255	  have ⟨g₁, hg₁_eq, hg₁_unique⟩ := h₁.exists_unique_ofCurve_comp h₁.ofCurve h₁.comp_ofCurve
   256	  have g₁_eq_id : g₁ = 𝟙 J₁ := by
   257	    refine (hg₁_unique (𝟙 J₁) ?_).symm
   258	    simp
   259	  have ggh_eq_g₁ : g ≫ h = g₁ := by
   260	    refine hg₁_unique (g ≫ h) ?_
   261	    change h₁.ofCurve = h₁.ofCurve ≫ (g ≫ h)
   262	    rw [← Category.assoc, ← hg_eq, ← hh_eq]
   263	  have hgh : g ≫ h = 𝟙 J₁ := by rw [ggh_eq_g₁, g₁_eq_id]
   264	  have ⟨k₂, hk₂_eq, hk₂_unique⟩ := h₂.exists_unique_ofCurve_comp h₂.ofCurve h₂.comp_ofCurve
   265	  have k₂_eq_id : k₂ = 𝟙 J₂ := by
   266	    refine (hk₂_unique (𝟙 J₂) ?_).symm
   267	    simp
   268	  have hhg_eq_k₂ : h ≫ g = k₂ := by
   269	    refine hk₂_unique (h ≫ g) ?_
   270	    change h₂.ofCurve = h₂.ofCurve ≫ (h ≫ g)
   271	    rw [← Category.assoc, ← hh_eq, ← hg_eq]
   272	  have hhg : h ≫ g = 𝟙 J₂ := by rw [hhg_eq_k₂, k₂_eq_id]
   273	  exact ⟨g, hg_eq, fun g' hg' => hg_unique g' hg'⟩
   274

   277	/-- A bundled Albanese witness for the smooth proper geometrically irreducible curve
   278	`C`: a candidate group scheme `J` (with proper, smooth, geometrically irreducible
   279	structure, smooth of relative dimension `genus C`), and a proof that `J` satisfies
   280	the Albanese universal property of Definition `IsAlbanese` for `C` *for every choice
   281	of $k$-rational marked point* `P : 𝟙_ _ ⟶ C`.
   282	
   283	Mathematically, the underlying scheme `J` (and its group/proper/smooth/irreducible
   284	structure) is intrinsic to `C`; only the universal morphism `C ⟶ J` depends on the
   285	choice of marked point `P`. Encoding `isAlbaneseFor` as a `∀ P, IsAlbanese …` field
   286	keeps the bundle independent of any specific pointing, which is what
   287	`AbelJacobi.Jacobian.ofCurve P` needs in order to project the Albanese morphism for
   288	an *arbitrary* input `P`.

   290	The smoothness witness is recorded at the specific relative dimension `genus C`,
   291	which is the form required by `Jacobian.smoothOfRelativeDimension_genus`. -/
   292	structure JacobianWitness (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
   293	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] where
   294	  /-- The candidate Albanese object. -/
   295	  J : Over (Spec (.of k))
   296	  /-- The group-scheme structure on `J`. -/
   297	  grpObj : GrpObj J
   298	  /-- `J` is proper over `k`. -/
   299	  proper : IsProper J.hom
   300	  /-- `J` is smooth over `k`. -/
   301	  smooth : Smooth J.hom
   302	  /-- `J` is geometrically irreducible over `k`. -/
   303	  geomIrred : GeometricallyIrreducible J.hom
   304	  /-- `J` is smooth of relative dimension `genus C` (so dim `J = genus C`). -/
   305	  smoothGenus : SmoothOfRelativeDimension (genus C) J.hom
   306	  /-- The Albanese universal-property data: for every choice of $k$-rational marked
   307	  point `P : 𝟙_ _ ⟶ C`, the scheme `J` together with its group/proper/smooth/irreducible
   308	  structure satisfies the Albanese universal property for the pointed curve `(C, P)`. -/
   309	  isAlbaneseFor : ∀ (P : 𝟙_ _ ⟶ C), @IsAlbanese k _ C P J grpObj proper smooth geomIrred

    12	# The Albanese universal property of `Pic⁰_{C/k̄}`, at the Jacobian
    13	
    14	`Albanese/AlbaneseFromData.lean` proves Milne Proposition III.6.1 over the
    15	symmetric-power interface in an arbitrary cartesian monoidal category. This file
    16	instantiates it at the object the challenge cares about: `J = Pic⁰_{C/k̄}` for a
    17	smooth proper geometrically irreducible curve `C` over an algebraically closed field.
    18	
    19	The point of the instantiation is that **every hypothesis of the general theorem is
    20	discharged here except one**. Specifically:
    21	
    22	* `IsCommMonObj (Pic0.jacobianScheme C)` and `IsCommMonObj A` — Milne §I.1 Corollary
    23	  1.4, now available on the project's four-instance package
    24	  (`isCommMonObj_of_isProper_smooth_of_package`, `Albanese/AVSelfProduct.lean`).
    25	* **pointed rigidity** for `Pic⁰ ⟶ A` — Milne §I.1 Corollary 1.2, likewise
    26	  (`isMonHom_of_pointed`). This is the `hom` input, and it rests on the sorry-free
    27	  rigidity chain of `RigidityLemma.lean`.
    28	* the connector in both directions, and the assembly — proved in
    29	  `Albanese/AlbaneseFromData.lean`.
    30	
    31	What is **not** discharged, and is the entire remaining content of this leg:
    32	
    33	> `SymPowData C (genus C)` — the `g`-th symmetric power of the curve, with its
    34	> symmetrisation projection and universal property,
    35	
    36	together with the cycle map presented as the symmetrisation of a pointed Abel–Jacobi
    37	map (`hf`, `haj0`) and the descent datum, which `Albanese/AlbaneseFromData.lean` §2
    38	reduces to a morphism on a dense open (Milne III.5.1(a) birationality).
    39	
    40	## Main result
    41	
    42	* `Pic0.albanese_universal_property_of_symPowData` — the Albanese universal property
    43	  of `Pic⁰_{C/k̄}`, with the symmetric power as an explicit argument. Axiom-clean
    44	  apart from what `Pic0.jacobianScheme` itself carries (see below).
    45	
    46	## An honest note on `sorryAx`
    47	
    48	`Pic0.jacobianScheme C` is built from `Pic0.bundle`, which routes through the Picard
    49	representability seam; at a *synthesis site* that seam still reports `sorryAx`
    50	(the five obligations named on the AJC team thread, none of them in this leg). So this
    51	theorem is **not** a closed result about the actual Jacobian, and must not be reported
    52	as one. What it does establish is sharp and worth stating precisely:
    53	
    54	> the Albanese *argument* is complete. Given the symmetric power, Milne III.6.1 holds
    55	> for `Pic⁰_{C/k̄}` with no further input from this leg.
    56	
    57	That is a different claim from `albanese_universal_property` in
    58	`Albanese/AlbaneseUP.lean`, which quantifies over a `sorry`-bodied `abelJacobi` and a
    59	`sorry`-bodied `SymmetricPower` and therefore asserts nothing about either.
    60	
    61	## References
    62	
    63	Milne, *Abelian Varieties*, §III.6 Proposition 6.1, p. 104; §I.1 Corollaries 1.2 and
    64	1.4. Blueprint `thm:albanese_universal_property`.
    65	-/

    84	/-- **The Albanese universal property of `Pic⁰_{C/k̄}` — Milne Proposition III.6.1,
    85	with the symmetric power supplied as data.**
    86	
    87	Let `C` be a smooth proper geometrically irreducible curve over an algebraically
    88	closed field `k̄`, let `A` be an abelian variety over `k̄`, and let `φ : C ⟶ A` be
    89	*pointed* at `P₀`. Suppose given
    90	
    91	* `D : SymPowData C (genus C)` — the `g`-th symmetric power with its symmetrisation
    92	  projection `π` and universal property, and the symmetry of `π` itself (`hproj`);
    93	* `f : Sym^g C ⟶ Pic⁰` presented as the symmetrisation of a pointed Abel–Jacobi map
    94	  `aj` (`hf : π ≫ f = aj(P₁) + ⋯ + aj(P_g)`, `haj0 : aj(P₀) = η_J`);
    95	* the descent datum `hdesc` — a unique `ψ` with `Sym^g φ = f ≫ ψ` (Milne's step 2,
    96	  reduced by `Albanese/AlbaneseFromData.lean` §2 to a morphism on a dense open of
    97	  `Pic⁰`).
    98	
    99	Then there is a **unique** `ψ : Pic⁰_{C/k̄} ⟶ A` with `φ = aj ≫ ψ`.
   100	
   101	Every other ingredient of Milne's proof is discharged in the body: commutativity of
   102	both group objects and pointed rigidity for `Pic⁰ ⟶ A` (Milne I.1.4 and I.1.2, via
   103	`Albanese/AVSelfProduct.lean`), and the connector in both directions
   104	(`Albanese/AlbaneseFromData.lean`). See the module header for why this is a statement
   105	about the Albanese *argument* rather than a closed result about the Jacobian. -/

   107	    (D : SymPowData C (genus C))
   108	    (hproj : ∀ σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin (genus C)),
   109	      permAut C σ ≫ D.proj = D.proj)
   110	    (P0 : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of kbar))) ⟶ C) (i₀ : Fin (genus C))
   111	    {A : Over (Spec (.of kbar))}
   112	    [GrpObj A] [IsProper A.hom] [Smooth A.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible A.hom]
   113	    (φ : C ⟶ A) (hφ : P0 ≫ φ = η[A])
   114	    (aj : C ⟶ jacobianScheme C) (f : D.carrier ⟶ jacobianScheme C)
   115	    (hf : letI := jacobianScheme_grpObj C
   116	      letI : IsCommMonObj (jacobianScheme C) := by
   117	        haveI := jacobianScheme_isProper C
   118	        haveI := jacobianScheme_smooth C
   119	        haveI := jacobianScheme_geomIrred C
   120	        exact isCommMonObj_of_isProper_smooth_of_package _
   121	      D.proj ≫ f = powSum (genus C) aj)
   122	    (haj0 : letI := jacobianScheme_grpObj C; P0 ≫ aj = η[jacobianScheme C])
   123	    (hdesc : letI := jacobianScheme_grpObj C
   124	      letI : IsCommMonObj A := isCommMonObj_of_isProper_smooth_of_package A
   125	      ∃! ψ : jacobianScheme C ⟶ A, D.symAVMap φ = f ≫ ψ) :
   126	    ∃! ψ : jacobianScheme C ⟶ A, φ = aj ≫ ψ := by
   127	  letI := jacobianScheme_grpObj C
   128	  haveI := jacobianScheme_isProper C
   129	  haveI := jacobianScheme_smooth C
   130	  haveI := jacobianScheme_geomIrred C
   131	  -- Milne I.1.4 for both group objects (`Albanese/AVSelfProduct.lean`).
   132	  letI : IsCommMonObj (jacobianScheme C) :=
   133	    isCommMonObj_of_isProper_smooth_of_package _
   134	  letI : IsCommMonObj A := isCommMonObj_of_isProper_smooth_of_package A
   135	  -- Milne I.1.2: a pointed morphism `Pic⁰ ⟶ A` is a homomorphism.
   136	  exact exists_unique_albanese_factorisation D f P0 i₀ hproj aj hf haj0 φ hφ
   137	    (fun ψ hψ => isMonHom_of_pointed ψ hψ) hdesc

   142	
   143	`Pic0.albanese_universal_property_of_symPowData` reports `sorryAx`, and it would be

   152	  -- [propext, sorryAx, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]

   155	The two differ only in the target group object. So the entire `sorryAx` residue of
   156	the specialised form is `Pic0.jacobianScheme` — i.e. the Picard representability seam
   157	upstream of this leg — and **none** of it is the Albanese argument. This is the

   165	/-- **The Albanese universal property with an arbitrary abelian variety as target.**
   166	
   167	Milne Proposition III.6.1 in its widest honest form: for *any* object `C`, any `g`,
   168	any symmetric-power datum `SymPowData C g`, and any two abelian varieties `J`, `A`
   169	over `k̄`, a pointed `φ : C ⟶ A` factors uniquely through a pointed `aj : C ⟶ J` whose
   170	symmetrisation is `f`, given the descent datum.
   171	
   172	Axiom-clean. Its role is twofold: it is the reusable statement (nothing about curves
   173	or the Jacobian is needed), and comparing its axiom set with that of
   174	`Pic0.albanese_universal_property_of_symPowData` attributes the latter's `sorryAx`
   175	entirely to the Picard seam. See the section note above. -/
   176	theorem albanese_universal_property_of_symPowData_generic
   177	    {kbar : Type u} [Field kbar] [IsAlgClosed kbar]
   178	    (C : Over (Spec (.of kbar))) (g : ℕ)
   179	    (D : SymPowData C g)
   180	    (hproj : ∀ σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin g), permAut C σ ≫ D.proj = D.proj)
   181	    (P0 : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of kbar))) ⟶ C) (i₀ : Fin g)
   182	    {J A : Over (Spec (.of kbar))}
   183	    [GrpObj J] [IsProper J.hom] [Smooth J.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible J.hom]
   184	    [GrpObj A] [IsProper A.hom] [Smooth A.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible A.hom]
   185	    (φ : C ⟶ A) (hφ : P0 ≫ φ = η[A])
   186	    (aj : C ⟶ J) (f : D.carrier ⟶ J)
   187	    (hf : letI : IsCommMonObj J := isCommMonObj_of_isProper_smooth_of_package J
   188	      D.proj ≫ f = powSum g aj)
   189	    (haj0 : P0 ≫ aj = η[J])
   190	    (hdesc : letI : IsCommMonObj A := isCommMonObj_of_isProper_smooth_of_package A
   191	      ∃! ψ : J ⟶ A, D.symAVMap φ = f ≫ ψ) :
   192	    ∃! ψ : J ⟶ A, φ = aj ≫ ψ := by
   193	  letI : IsCommMonObj J := isCommMonObj_of_isProper_smooth_of_package J
   194	  letI : IsCommMonObj A := isCommMonObj_of_isProper_smooth_of_package A
   195	  exact exists_unique_albanese_factorisation D f P0 i₀ hproj aj hf haj0 φ hφ
   196	    (fun ψ hψ => isMonHom_of_pointed ψ hψ) hdesc
   197
